verdict.rationale: Floot's docs describe an assistant that takes delegated work. Users can point at an element or annotate a screenshot for the assistant to pick up, describe an integration and have endpoints, tables and screens built, ask it to restore a checkpoint, or say "make this a mobile app." Much of the documentation, however, frames the assistant as an external AI chat (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) connected over MCP, so the depth of a truly built-in, in-product assistant is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: clear first-party documentation of the native in-editor assistant's scope and task-delegation flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration of in-product delegation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: point at an element or annotate a screenshot for the assistant to pick up
Describe the integration you want to your AI assistant, and the endpoints, database tables, and screens get built for you.
Ask it to restore a checkpoint from before the change went sideways.
Take any website you've built on Floot and say "make this a mobile app."
